question: Walk through how you debug an intermittent bug that only happens for some users.
shortAnswer: Reproduce or collect signals, form a hypothesis, change one variable, verify with logs/metrics/tests.
strongAnswer: Gather environment differences (locale, OS version, feature flags, data shape). Add request/user correlation IDs. Form a falsifiable hypothesis (e.g., null field on legacy accounts). Instrument narrowly, avoid shotgun logging. Fix root cause and add a regression test when feasible.
followUps: What if you cannot reproduce locally?
How do you avoid fixing only the symptom?
commonWrongAnswer: Restart the server and change three unrelated configs at once until it stops.
productionRelevance: Intermittent auth and locale bugs are common; structured debugging separates seniors from guessers.
integrationProcedure: 1) Reproduce the scenario in a small spike using debugging. 2) Write the strong answer as an ADR or PR description. 3) Add a test or monitor that would catch the common wrong answer in production. 4) Document rollback/owner. 5) Rehearse the follow-ups aloud once.
